Daily Brief

The day's headlines are dominated by escalating tensions between Washington and Kyiv, as Ukraine accused the US of disrupting Starlink satellite services critical to its drone operations, with Elon Musk suggesting the US government controls any restrictions [BBC, Globe and Mail, RFI]. President Zelensky announced Ukraine would resume strikes on Russian refineries after what he called a failed 'energy ceasefire' unilaterally declared by President Trump [Al Jazeera, Globe and Mail]. In Europe, EU leaders convene for contentious budget negotiations worth nearly two trillion euros, racing to reach agreement before France's presidential election amid fears of eurosceptic gains [France 24, RFI]. Asian markets suffered sharp losses, with the KOSPI falling over 7% and the Nikkei down 4%, triggered by higher-than-expected US inflation data and AI investment concerns [Nikkei Asia]. Tragic news from Pakistan where at least 17 children and a teacher were killed in a school roof collapse in Peshawar [The Hindu, Al Jazeera]. Meanwhile, China and North Korea opened a long-delayed border bridge, signaling deepening ties between the Cold War-era allies [Nikkei Asia, France 24, Al Jazeera].

01 Conflict

Ukraine Reports Starlink Disruptions as Musk Points to US Government Control

  • Ukraine reported that Starshield, the military-grade SpaceX satellite system, imposed speed limits of 100mph on Tuesday night, disrupting drone attack missions and air defense operations
  • Elon Musk stated on X that Starshield systems are owned and controlled by the US government, with limits decided by the US military and ultimately the president
  • President Zelensky called the disruptions 'a big mistake' that 'will bring a lot of human losses' and appealed for service restoration
  • Partial connectivity was restored by Wednesday evening according to Ukraine's former defence minister Mykhailo Fedorov

Ukraine Resumes Strikes on Russian Refineries After Failed Energy Ceasefire

  • President Zelensky told the Financial Times that Ukraine was 'done' with the energy ceasefire and would resume attacks on Russian oil refineries
  • Russia reported a Ukrainian drone strike on an oil refinery in Ryazan, about 180km south of Moscow, causing a fire
  • Trump had unilaterally announced an energy ceasefire on Sunday, but Russia continued striking Ukrainian energy infrastructure, leaving 600,000 Ukrainians without power
  • Zelensky criticized Trump's 'favouritism toward Russia' and expressed frustration at alleged withdrawal of US intelligence sharing

03 Geopolitics

EU Leaders Face High-Stakes Budget Showdown Ahead of French Election

  • EU leaders meet Thursday to negotiate the bloc's next long-term budget covering 2028-2034, worth nearly two trillion euros
  • Leaders are racing to reach agreement by December, fearing eurosceptic wins in upcoming elections, particularly France's presidential vote
  • Marine Le Pen, frontrunner in the French election, called it a 'democratic scandal' to adopt a budget before next year's votes and wants to slash France's EU contribution
  • Key disputes include funding levels for agriculture, defense, economic competitiveness versus US and China, and migration return hubs in Africa

At Least 17 Children Killed in Pakistan School Roof Collapse

  • The roof of a private school collapsed in Dir Colony, inner-city Peshawar, on Thursday morning
